scope: Different-author, read-only and source-only fail-closed hammer of the sealed M1862 additive C2 K8 case0 mapped public-fault X/Z diagnostic successor. The review verifies the exact source inventory, contract and author double seals, M1857 failed-predecessor chain, docs/359, namespace absence, CPython 3.6/3.12 checker and tests, all twelve M1857 synchronized-inventory mutations, and four additional direct-control-flow mutations. No simulator, EDA executable, license query, attempt, result, release, source mutation, predecessor mutation, docs/359 mutation, ucli.key access, commit, or push was performed.
verdict: FAIL CLOSED. M1862's exact checked-in runner and testbench are narrowly scoped and the original twelve M1857 escape classes are now rejected on both required Python runtimes. However, the semantic checker still accepts synchronized-inventory mutations that retain a counted critical node or token inside a constant-false branch: verify_authority(), ATTEMPT.mkdir(), the only compile run(), and the first $finish. Consequently its AST/cardinality checks do not prove that authorization, attempt consumption, the unique compile, or first-X/Z termination are executable on the actual control path. M1864 must not be created. An additive successor must require critical runner statements as direct statements in the expected main/run blocks and reject constant/dead control ancestors; it must also structurally require each $finish as the direct unconditional terminal statement of its stop task. The four attacks must be synchronized and rejected under CPython 3.6 and 3.12 before a new review/release chain.

findings.title: Critical authorization, attempt, compile, and diagnostic-stop nodes can be made unreachable without failing the checker
findings.evidence: With each mutated source SHA synchronized into contract.source_files, the checker accepted four attacks on both CPython 3.6 and 3.12: guarding verify_authority(), ATTEMPT.mkdir(), or the sole compile run() by Python if False, and guarding the first SystemVerilog $finish by if (1'b0). The exact twelve M1857 mutations were all rejected, so this is not stale inventory or a replay of the predecessor defect.
findings.impact: A future release would rely on a checker that can approve a source where authority is bypassed, attempt consumption or the one compile is absent at runtime, or first-X/Z localization prints without terminating. That violates the fail-closed launch and diagnostic contracts.
findings.required_fix: Use an additive successor rather than mutating sealed M1862. Bind the critical main/run sequence to direct statement-list positions (no If/Try/With/loop/lambda ancestors), bind run calls to direct assignments/statements and exact executable order, and parse stop-task statement structure so each matching display is followed by a direct unconditional $finish. Add these four synchronized mutations to both-runtime tests. Require a new different-author review and a new double-sealed release label; do not issue M1864 from M1862.
